why.T3-001: The room's own members post fakes as true for April Fools (the AMD-unapproved petition, claims that Intel/NVIDIA are better, a moderator's fake resignation to Nvidiayy) and others reply inside them (checking the petition, 'you just got bamboozled', posting the sub's own AF joke); nothing shows the whole sub renamed or restyled as the joke's stage, so T3-023's gate is not met.

why.T3-084: The codes are requests from one canvas room to another, as a group, for help with its work — UVic asking SFU to help spruce up its logo and SFU asking a visiting VIU member 'can you help us?' — rather than a call carried into kindred subs' membership (T3-062) or pixels sent unasked to a neighbour's defence (T3-011).

why.T3-005: The codes rally the room against Blue's announced invasion and answer it with calls to DEFEND, retake and refuse surrender — an attack under way and the room's fight — rather than routine watching and fixing with no fight called (T3-021).

why.T3-121: Asking the mods to BAN HIM is exclusion used as the room's sanction against someone harming blue, the policing act the item names; naming a culprit and asking for art to stop are its background (T3-087, T3-008), which do not carry the sanctioning itself.

why.T3-169: The codes design, add, repair and defend the r/cubers tag stuck below the cube — the sub's name written on the canvas — so the doing is signing, not counting newcomers the mark brings (T3-044), which is only the tag's stated purpose.

why.T3-037: The codes weigh the canvas effort itself — 'I couldn't care less' against refusing to stop other fans having fun — debating the room's showing, not canvas posts crowding the sub (T3-075).

why.T3-050: A hostile post taunts the farmers for their loss and the room later celebrates the carrot-themed replies it drew — a taunt exchange with a rival and its answer, not the room's own running in-joke played among members (T3-031).

why.T3-006: The codes nominate, direct and rally attacks on named artworks, flags, coordinates and communities — 'Attack the F1 logo', 'Consume the American flag', 'Destroy the communist hammer and sickle' — the attacks themselves, so the target is the point rather than a colour spread for its own sake (T3-171).

why.T3-009: The codes mark the room's own finished logo as achieved — 'nicely unvandalsavageized. Go team!', glad Batman was fixed before the canvas ended, the logo cleaned up — celebration of the work, not a plain account of what happened to it (T3-073).

why.T3-033: The lead is offering the room the idea of putting r/signal on r/place and asking who is in, before any picture is chosen — proposing the room's mark and calling it to make it, not hands called to an already chosen picture (T3-002).

why.T3-174: The codes are the Void faction performing its own membership — hails, creeds, blessings, anthems, personification and declarations of belonging ('All Hail The Void', 'WE ARE LEGION', 'I am now part of nothing') — professing loyalty to the colour as faith, not any running in-joke of the room (T3-031).

why.T3-150: The codes name an alliance (r/cubers in alliance with r/bulgaria), accept it, and list mutual respect and protection agreements with neighbours — rooms joining for joint defence of their borders, so the deal kind is the alliance rather than a bare border settlement (T3-010).
